post.description:
Send one SMS through the organization's messaging route.

Everything refusable is refused before the provider is touched — an
undialable number, no active route, a route with no sender — and those
leave no row. A provider rejection *does* leave one, marked ``failed``
with the vendor's own wording, because "unverified destination" and
"blocked as spam" need different fixes and both deserve a record.

The 201 carries the message as of acceptance (``sent``). Re-read it for
the delivery verdict.

get.description:
Point to one call attempt's recording (VOAD-37).

This serves whatever ``CallAttempt.recording_url`` already holds — it does
not itself record anything. As of this change nothing in the call engine
(``src.application.engine.session.CallSession``) captures audio at all:
there is no recording processor/observer anywhere in the pipeline, so
``recording_url`` is NULL for every attempt today. Wiring real capture
(e.g. Pipecat's ``AudioBufferProcessor``, uploaded to storage and this
column set to the resulting URL) touches the live engine/pipeline and is
out of scope here — see the deployment notes for that follow-up.

Never a 500 for a legitimately recording-less attempt: a missing call or
attempt, an attempt that never connected, and an attempt with nothing
stored yet are each a 404 with a detail message that says which.

CallDirectionEnum.title: CallDirectionEnum
CallDirectionEnum.description: Who placed the call. Decides whether the agent speaks first.

CallLifecycleEnum.title: CallLifecycleEnum
CallLifecycleEnum.description:
One call-as-assignment across all of its attempts.

``calling`` means an attempt exists that has not settled yet; the
dispatcher settles it back to ``pending`` (retry scheduled) or forward to
a terminal state. ``exhausted`` is "we tried, per policy, and never got a
conversation" — distinct from ``completed``, which means one happened.

CallOutcomeEnum.title: CallOutcomeEnum
CallOutcomeEnum.description:
The business result of a conversation, distinct from the technical
attempt status. Assigned by post-call analysis (``services/analysis.py``);
``no_answer`` (telephony) and ``sms_sent`` (a delivered/sent ``Message``)
are the exceptions — derived, no LLM involved.

CallStatusEnum.title: CallStatusEnum
CallStatusEnum.description:
Where a call is in its life, as campaign logic needs to see it.

Coarser than SIP: a retry policy cares whether the callee was busy, absent,
or spoken to — not which of three provisional responses preceded that.

CallingHours.title: CallingHours
CallingHours.description:
When a campaign is allowed to make phones ring.

Evaluated on the wall clock of ``timezone`` by default — the campaign's
market, not the server's locale. Unset ``start``/``end`` means any time
of day; ``weekdays`` uses Python's convention (0 = Monday).

VOAD-33: a call's window is actually evaluated on the timezone derived
from its client's country (``utils.timezone.country_to_timezone``), not
this ``timezone`` field — callers pass that derived zone in explicitly
via ``is_open``/``is_priority``'s ``timezone`` argument. ``timezone``
remains the fallback for calls whose client has no resolvable country,
which is also exactly the pre-VOAD-33 behavior for a campaign whose
clients carry no country data at all.

CampaignStatusEnum.title: CampaignStatusEnum
CampaignStatusEnum.description:
Where a campaign is in its life. Operators drive it; the dispatcher
moves ``scheduled → running`` and ``running → completed`` on its own,
and can also move a campaign to ``error`` when its setup becomes
undialable at runtime (VOAD-36) — distinct from ``paused``, which is an
operator's deliberate choice.

ChunkingConfig.title: ChunkingConfig
ChunkingConfig.description:
How the reply is cut on its way to TTS.

Each chunk is a separate synthesis request, and a request is an independent
draw of the speaker, so chunk count trades latency against how much the
voice can drift inside one answer. ``clause_cuts`` is the compromise: only
the chunks on the latency path may be cut at a clause, the rest run to a
sentence end.

ChunkingModeEnum.title: ChunkingModeEnum
ChunkingModeEnum.description:
How a reply is cut up on its way to TTS.

``clause`` speaks the first clause while the model is still generating, and
is what keeps time-to-first-audio under a second. ``whole_turn`` waits for
the complete reply and synthesises it in one request: one draw of the
speaker, so the voice cannot drift mid-answer, paid for in latency.

ClientSegmentEnum.title: ClientSegmentEnum
ClientSegmentEnum.description:
A client's lead temperature, distinct from :class:`ClientStatusEnum`
(which gates whether the client may be dialed at all). Assigned by a
status-column CSV import (VOAD-32); has no bearing on ``do_not_call``.

ClientStatusEnum.title: ClientStatusEnum
ClientStatusEnum.description:
Whether a client may be dialed. Anything but ``active`` is refused at
upload, at originate, and again by the dispatcher at claim time.

FragmentParams.title: FragmentParams
FragmentParams.description:
What a ceiling commit is allowed to send to the LLM.

An utterance cut at ``max_delay_ms`` may be half a sentence. Answering half
a sentence is worse than asking the caller to go on, so a commit that looks
unfinished is re-prompted instead.

LanguageConfig.title: LanguageConfig
LanguageConfig.description:
What differs for one language.

Every field is optional: unset means "use the agent's default". The merge in
:func:`resolve_profile` replaces whole sections, so a language that wants a
different ceiling supplies a whole :class:`TurnParams`.

LanguageSwitchPolicy.title: LanguageSwitchPolicy
LanguageSwitchPolicy.description:
Whether a caller's detected language may retarget a live call.

Off by default: a switch rewrites the prompt layers, which burns the prefix
cache once, so it is an explicit organization choice rather than a surprise.
Only languages the agent has configured (or its default) are candidates —
switching to a language with no row would change the voice and nothing
else, which is the half-switched call this policy exists to prevent.

The detection signal comes from the recogniser
(``BaseSttAdapter.detected_language``). Backends that never report one
(``SttCapabilities.reports_language`` false) leave the whole mechanism
inert regardless of this policy.

MessageStatusEnum.title: MessageStatusEnum
MessageStatusEnum.description:
Where an outbound SMS is in its life.

Coarser than any one vendor's vocabulary, and ordered: a status callback
may only move a message **forward** through this list. Carriers deliver
dispositions out of order often enough that "sent" arriving after
"delivered" is routine, not an anomaly, and the later write must lose.

The distinction that matters operationally is ``undelivered`` vs
``failed``: the carrier accepted the message and could not deliver it
(handset off, number dead) vs the provider never got it off the ground
(no route, blocked, bad sender). One is the destination's problem, the
other is the configuration's.

ModelConfig.title: ModelConfig
ModelConfig.description:
A served model, plus the parts of its behaviour the engine must know.

``capabilities`` overrides what the adapter class declares. It exists
because the same client code faces servers that disagree about the protocol
they implement — one Qwen3-ASR deployment finalises on a newline, a Voxtral
deployment goes quiet instead — and those differences belong in data, where
an operator can correct them, rather than in a branch nobody can reach.

PriorityInterval.title: PriorityInterval
PriorityInterval.description:
A sub-window of the calling day (VOAD-33) that earns priority dialing.

Evaluated on the same local clock as the enclosing :class:`CallingHours`
— the campaign's own timezone, or a per-call one derived from the
client's country. A lead whose local time falls inside one of these earns
a dial before leads that are merely inside the general window.

PromptSet.title: PromptSet
PromptSet.description:
The three LLM-facing strings that make up a call, in one language.

Written natively per language rather than translated at runtime: a model
follows an instruction in the language it is answering in far more reliably,
and a fixed string is prefix-cacheable where a generated one is not.

ProviderConfig.title: ProviderConfig
ProviderConfig.description:
Where a model is served and how to authenticate to it.

One organization's Voxtral and another's are different endpoints with
different keys, so this is per-call data rather than deployment config, and
a client built from it must never be shared between calls.

ProviderKindEnum.title: ProviderKindEnum
ProviderKindEnum.description: Which side of the pipeline a provider serves.

ReasonCategoryEnum.title: ReasonCategoryEnum
ReasonCategoryEnum.description: Why a ``not_interested`` conversation ended that way.

ResolvedProfile.title: ResolvedProfile
ResolvedProfile.description:
One call's settings after the merge — what the pipeline is built from.

Deliberately flat. Everything downstream reads this and never the layers it
came from, so a call's behaviour can be logged, diffed, and replayed as one
object.

RetryPolicy.title: RetryPolicy
RetryPolicy.description:
What a failed attempt earns: another try later, or the end of the road.

``max_attempts`` counts every attempt including the first. A status with
no delay here (completed, canceled) is not retried — a conversation that
happened is done, and a cancel was somebody's decision.

SAudienceUploadHistoryRead.title: SAudienceUploadHistoryRead
SAudienceUploadHistoryRead.description:
One persisted upload event (VOAD-34's "История загрузок") — distinct
from :class:`SAudienceUploadRead`, which is the immediate per-request
result and is never stored.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Amount to add to the balance

SCallAttemptDetailsRead.title: SCallAttemptDetailsRead
SCallAttemptDetailsRead.description: An attempt with its transcript — what the caller actually heard.

SMessageRead.title: SMessageRead
SMessageRead.description:
A sent message and wherever the carrier's verdict has got to.

``status`` is ``sent`` right after the provider accepts it; delivery
callbacks move it to ``delivered``, ``undelivered`` or ``failed``
afterwards, so a caller who needs the verdict re-reads this row.

SSessionRead.title: SSessionRead
SSessionRead.description: What login / refresh / me / change_organization answer with.

SVoiceAgentDetailsRead.title: SVoiceAgentDetailsRead
SVoiceAgentDetailsRead.description: Agent plus its language rows — the full layer-1 + layer-2 picture.

SVoiceRead.title: SVoiceRead
SVoiceRead.description: One voice from a TTS model's live catalogue (see ``GET /models/{id}/voices``).

SentimentEnum.title: SentimentEnum
SentimentEnum.description: The tone of a meaningful conversation, assigned by post-call analysis.

SilencePolicy.title: SilencePolicy
SilencePolicy.description: How long to tolerate a caller saying nothing, and what to do about it.

SmsMessageStatusEnum.title: SmsMessageStatusEnum
SmsMessageStatusEnum.description:
Moderation state of a VoiceAgent's fixed SMS-tool text (VOAD-62).

Not to be confused with ``MessageStatusEnum`` above, which tracks a sent
message's delivery — this tracks whether the *configured text itself* is
cleared to be sent at all. Text written or edited by staff starts
``pending`` and cannot be sent (the tool isn't even offered to the model)
until an owner/admin/super_admin approves it; text written by
owner/admin/super_admin is ``approved`` immediately.

SpokenPrompts.title: SpokenPrompts
SpokenPrompts.description:
Lines the agent speaks without asking the LLM.

Localised per language, and deliberately not model output: they must be
instant, identical every time, and safe to say when the model is unreachable.

TttConfig-Input.title: TttConfig
TttConfig-Input.description: The LLM, and the sampling it runs with.

TttConfig-Output.title: TttConfig
TttConfig-Output.description: The LLM, and the sampling it runs with.

TurnAnalyzerEnum.title: TurnAnalyzerEnum
TurnAnalyzerEnum.description: End-of-turn classifiers consulted by the turn controller.

TurnParams.title: TurnParams
TurnParams.description:
When a pause becomes the caller's turn ending.

The cascade: below ``min_delay_ms`` the caller is almost certainly
mid-breath and an inference is wasted; between min and max the analyzer is
asked every ``repoll_ms``; at ``max_delay_ms`` the turn commits regardless.
The ceiling is load-bearing, not a safety net — it is what stops a caller
who trails off from being ignored.

VadAdapterEnum.title: VadAdapterEnum
VadAdapterEnum.description: Voice activity detectors. In-process, no endpoint.

VadConfig.title: VadConfig
VadConfig.description: Voice activity detection. Runs in-process on every frame.
